channel.title: Daily Perspective
channel.description: A daily digest of tech, world, economy and perspective.

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
item.description: Behind each headline—AI lawsuits, cyber threats, ceasefires, budgets—are people making sense of uncertainty. Whose perspective haven't you considered today, and what might they need you to understand?

item.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
item.description: Behind every infrastructure cost and buyout headline is someone recalculating their life. Can you hold the systemic story and the individual one at the same time, without letting either erase the other?

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
item.description: Behind every layoff statistic and IPO headline is a person recalculating their life—just as behind every conflict report is someone rebuilding theirs. Whose perspective are you missing today?

item.title: Sunday, October 25, 2026
item.description: Before reacting to today's headlines, ask: whose daily survival is reduced to a data point here—and what would the story look like told from inside their life, not above it?

item.title: Saturday, October 24, 2026
item.description: Behind every data policy and border tariff is someone's daily life being quietly reshaped—whose perspective are you missing when a headline feels abstract rather than personal?

item.title: Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center's power bill and every ceasefire rumor is someone whose daily life hangs on decisions made far away. Whose perspective are you missing today?

item.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center's water use, every blocked port, every drone strike statistic, there's someone whose daily life just got harder. What would today's news look like written from their perspective instead of ours?

item.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026
item.description: Policy debates and inflation numbers are abstractions until you remember each one lands on someone harvesting olives, fleeing a drone, or counting grocery receipts—whose eyes would change how you read today's headlines?

item.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
item.description: Behind every data point—displaced Yemenis, hungry families, AI-disrupted jobs—is someone navigating uncertainty you'll never face. What would change if policy debates started with their names, not statistics?

item.title: Monday, October 19, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline about AI governance or infrastructure failure are people who built something fragile by hand—much like the half-million in Gaza facing winter without food. Scale shifts; vulnerability doesn't.

item.title: Sunday, October 18, 2026
item.description: Behind today's headlines on surveillance, sanctions, and budgets are people adapting to forces beyond their control—whether a warehouse worker, a displaced family, or a miner. What would today's news look like through their eyes, not just the systems'?

item.title: Saturday, October 17, 2026
item.description: Sudan's famine and Ethiopia-Eritrea's tension get a fraction of the attention Ukraine or Gaza receive—worth asking why some suffering feels more visible to you than other suffering, and what that quiet hierarchy costs the people living it.

item.title: Friday, October 16, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline—olive groves destroyed, a collapsed school, a contested data policy—are people navigating systems built without them in mind. Whose perspective is missing from the story you just read?

item.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026
item.description: Behind every policy debate—AI hiring algorithms, inflation numbers, ceasefire terms—are people making impossible choices with incomplete information, much like the Afghan parents facing drought. What would you need to feel safe enough to hope?

item.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026
item.description: Yazidi women clearing the same mines that nearly killed them — what does it mean to make peace with a landscape that once meant only terror?

item.title: Tuesday, October 13, 2026
item.description: Behind every headline - a shrinking safe zone, a bankrupt startup, a strained budget - is someone adjusting their whole life to a decision they didn't make. Whose adjustment are you overlooking today?

item.title: Monday, October 12, 2026
item.description: 117 million displaced people rarely choose fragility—it's imposed by war, drought, or policy. Before scrolling past, ask: whose daily survival depends on decisions made far from where they stand?

item.title: Sunday, October 11, 2026
item.description: Who decides when your political future gets postponed, your data center's impact gets hidden, or your documentation goes unread? Power often means never having to explain yourself to those most affected.

item.title: Saturday, October 10, 2026
item.description: Behind each headline—an AI's false tip, a displaced family under drone fire, a worker bound by a restrictive contract—is someone whose full story you haven't heard. What would change if you asked for it?

item.title: Friday, October 9, 2026
item.description: Behind each data point is a person: a laid-off safety researcher, a displaced Sudanese family, a farmer guarding his land. What would today's headlines feel like if you were the one living inside them?

item.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026
item.description: Behind today's headlines on AI claims, visa policies, and market shifts are people rarely asked for input—displaced families, regulated workers, cafeteria students. Whose perspective is missing from the decisions you'll make today?

item.title: Wednesday, October 7, 2026
item.description: Behind each headline—a missile strike, a job cut, a risky confession—is someone whose day looks nothing like yours. What would change if you tried to see it through their eyes before forming an opinion?

item.title: Tuesday, October 6, 2026
item.description: Behind every disrupted border, licensing fee, and market swing is someone whose daily life just got harder — whose version of today's news would read entirely differently than yours.

item.title: Monday, October 5, 2026
item.description: Infrastructure, borders, and algorithms all fail quietly until a person feels it first—whose daily strain today might you be missing because the system still looks fine from where you sit?

item.title: Sunday, October 4, 2026
item.description: Behind every jobs report and policy debate are individuals—laid-off workers, aid workers in conflict zones, engineers questioning their industry's direction. What would today's headlines look like if written from their vantage point instead of ours?

item.title: Saturday, October 3, 2026
item.description: Behind each data-center protest, layoff statistic, and conflict headline is someone adapting with limited power. What would today's news look like if it centered their resourcefulness instead of just the systems acting upon them?

item.title: Friday, October 2, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center squeeze, jobs report, and conflict headline are people adjusting their lives in real time—whose daily reality today are you assuming too quickly you understand?

item.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026
item.description: Behind every policy debate—AI oversight, trade disputes, energy prices—are people absorbing the consequences. Whose daily life changes because of decisions made far from where they live?

item.title: Wednesday, September 30, 2026
item.description: Policies and products are designed at a distance from the people they affect—whose daily life would look different if you had to live inside the systems you build or approve?

item.title: Tuesday, September 29, 2026
item.description: Behind every efficiency metric—grid uptime, AI agents, facial recognition scans—there's a person unaccounted for. Whose burden are you not seeing in today's systems, and what would it take to notice them?
